spec.name: odin-landing-lead
spec.type: Marketing landing page with lead-capture contact form
spec.stack: Next.js (App Router, React, API route for form submit) + Prisma + PostgreSQL, deployed to the Azure VM (django-vm, resource group DJANGO-PROJECT) behind the existing nginx/systemd setup
spec.description: Build a SMALL landing page with a contact form that saves leads to a database, and deploy it when finished. This is build iteration 'rep 2'. Scope: a single responsive landing page (hero/value copy + CTA) containing a contact form that captures lead fields (name, email, message, and timestamp). On submit, a server-side API route validates the input and PERSISTS each lead as a row in a PostgreSQL database via Prisma (table e.g. Lead). The page runs as a Next.js app built inside its OWN project folder (workspace/projects/odin-landing-lead) — never scaffolded at the Odin repo root. After the build is verified locally (page renders, form POST returns 200, a lead row is actually written), DEPLOY it to the Azure VM: firewall refreshed to the owner's current public IP via the Azure control plane (port 22 single-IP; 80/443 stay open), then rsync/build/migrate/restart over SSH as user mostafa (NEVER as root), excluding all secrets/backups (.env*, .backup-env, *.pem, *.key, *.bak, *.tmp, *.copy, config/*.json). Migrations use `prisma migrate deploy` only (additive). Explicit owner instruction: NO QA agent on this project. Deploy is a real state change and must be proposed with exact commands + impact + rollback and approved before execution; after deploy, poll the URL until HTTP 200 before reporting online.
features: Responsive single-page landing (hero, value proposition, CTA)
Contact form with fields: name, email, message
Client + server-side validation of form input
Server API route that writes each submission to the database
PostgreSQL `Lead` table (name, email, message, created_at) via Prisma schema + migration
Confirmation/success state after a successful submit
Deploy to the Azure VM (build, migrate deploy, restart via systemd) once verified

features.name: Basic spam protection (honeypot field or rate limit)
features.why: A public lead form will attract bot submissions; a honeypot is cheap and keeps the Lead table clean. Not building unless you approve.

features.name: Lead notification email on submit
features.why: Email the owner (via the connected Klaviyo/Email path) when a new lead arrives so leads aren't missed — optional, needs an Email operator if you want it.

members.name: Designer
members.why: Could sharpen the landing page's visual/brand polish beyond a clean default. Not staffed unless you want design work — Fullstack ships a tidy standard layout otherwise.
